notes: Titles and DOIs verified against acquired full texts. Original acquired as full PMC HTML; replication acquired as publisher PDF hosted by an author. Original reference uses 2015 online year, while replication cites its 2016 issue year. Both sides examined and sample sizes verified by test degrees of freedom. target_match remains unknown because the neutral description and page locators do not uniquely specify a statistical test. No metric conversion performed. Original Experiment 2 Recall Memory candidate omnibus tests: valence F(2,88)=24.032, p<.001, partial eta-squared=.353; Cue Type by Valence F(2,88)=18.362, p<.001, partial eta-squared=.294; three-way interaction F(2,88)=4.036, p=.021, partial eta-squared=.084. Background-only item-cue comparisons also differ by cue order and valence (first-cue negative versus neutral t(44)=6.247, p<.001; positive versus neutral t(44)=3.842, p<.001; second-cue negative versus neutral t(44)=5.276, p<.001). Replication PDF p.8/journal p.967 candidate tests: unconditioned valence F(2,52)=4.66, p=.014, partial eta-squared=.152; Target by Valence F(2,52)=3.95, p=.025, partial eta-squared=.132; conditionalized valence F(2,52)=6.50, p=.003, partial eta-squared=.200. Background-only unconditioned comparisons are positive versus neutral t(26)=3.65, p<.001 and negative versus neutral t(26)=3.22, p<.001, without printed partial eta-squared. These alternatives are retained here rather than assigning an arbitrary candidate to the singular es/p fields. Author narrative verdict concerns replication of the cued-recall finding generally, rather than one uniquely specified contrast.
